proposed.explanation:
You asked me to estimate Abu Qir's (ABUK) full-year 2026 EPS and compare it with Edita's (EFID) 2025 EPS. Here is what the evidence supports:

**ABUK – 9-month 2026 EPS (verified):** 8.74 EGP per share for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, up from 4.28 EGP in the same period a year earlier (a roughly 104 % increase, though the exact percentage figure is flagged AMBIGUOUS in the OCR).

**Estimating full-year 2026 EPS:** I only have a verified 9-month figure. The Q3-2026 standalone EPS (1.99 EGP) is marked AMBIGUOUS, so I cannot rely on it for a precise Q4 proxy. Using the verified Q3-2025 EPS of 1.23 EGP as a conservative stand-in for Q4-2026 gives a lower-bound estimate of 8.74 + 1.23 ≈ 9.97 EGP. A simple 12/9 annualisation of the 9-month figure gives 8.74 × 12/9 ≈ 11.65 EGP. A reasonable planning range is therefore roughly 10–12 EGP per share for FY 2026. This is an estimate, not a forecast; actual Q4 results could differ materially.

**EFID – FY 2025 EPS (verified):** 2.18 EGP per share for the year ended 31 December 2025, up from 1.09 EGP in 2024.

**Comparison:** Even at the conservative end of the range (~10 EGP), ABUK's estimated FY 2026 EPS is roughly 4–5× EFID's FY 2025 EPS of 2.18 EGP. On this single metric, Abu Qir clearly beats Edita.

**Why I recommend keep_cash rather than a buy:** Your stated goal is to compare the two exporters, and you currently hold no shares. The evidence provided covers only one metric (EPS) for each company. A responsible 5-year investment decision also requires valuation context (P/E, P/B), balance-sheet strength, dividend policy, sector and currency risk, and a view on whether the EPS growth is sustainable. None of that is in the evidence set. I would not commit your 35,000 EGP on EPS alone. Continue your research; when you are ready to allocate, the diversification cap (no single stock > 50 % of portfolio value) will apply.

**Risks and caveats:** The ABUK estimate is a rough extrapolation from 9 months of data; Q4 could be weaker or stronger. The AMBIGUOUS Q3-2026 figure means I could not confirm the most recent quarterly run-rate. EFID's 2025 EPS is a full-year audited figure, so the comparison is not perfectly like-for-like (9-month annualised vs. full-year). This is guidance, not a guarantee of future performance.
